page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6e.13xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. The instance features 52 physical cores with 1 thread per core, providing 52 dedicated vCPUs. It is configured with 96.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 1.85 GB per core. This hardware configuration does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 16 Gbps, and virtualization is managed via the KVM hypervisor.

Benchmark results position this instance primarily in the average tier for multi-core operations, while single-core performance is relatively weak. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance is rated in the bottom 25% at 1311.39, and single-threaded gzip compression is similarly weak at 22.9 GB/sec. However, multi-core capabilities show moderate throughput, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 45505.98 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 11386.0, both falling within the middle 50% of tested servers. Memory bandwidth is stable, recording 101.16 GB/sec for large block read-only operations and 36.51 GB/sec for large block write operations.

Given the high core count relative to the memory capacity, the instance is structured for compute-heavy workloads that can leverage parallel processing without requiring massive memory footprints. Appropriate workloads include multi-threaded software compilation, ray tracing, and static web serving, where the instance achieves a throughput of 22.62 GB/sec. The lack of bundled local storage and weak single-core performance are key tradeoffs, making it less suitable for single-threaded tasks or applications requiring high-speed local disk I/O. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the instance offers a high density of dedicated physical cores, making it a viable option for parallelized CPU tasks that do not justify the higher cost of memory-optimized hardware.
